brief: ALCHEMY SAND: a falling-sand chemistry sandbox (cellular automaton) where elements fall, flow, burn, melt and react. Grid around 320x200 cells (fewer on phones), typed arrays, updated bottom-up with alternating left/right scan order to avoid directional bias, rendered through ImageData with per-cell colour noise so materials look textured, scaled up crisp with image-rendering: pixelated. At least 16 elements with distinct behaviour: sand, wet sand, water, salt, saltwater, stone, wood, plant (grows into water), fire, smoke, steam, lava, basalt, ice (melts near heat, slowly freezes neighbouring water), oil (floats on water, very flammable), acid (dissolves most solids and is used up), gunpowder (explodes with a radial blast that throws particles), metal, plus an eraser. At least 20 reactions, e.g. water + lava -> basalt + steam; fire + wood -> fire, ash, smoke; salt + water -> saltwater; acid + metal -> flammable gas; steam condenses back to water near the top; plant spreads into water; oil burns with dark smoke. Density-based displacement (heavier sinks through lighter liquids and gases). A simple temperature field is a plus. UI: element palette with swatches and short names grouped (Solids, Powders, Liquids, Gases, Energy); brush size; spray mode; pause; step one tick; clear; a Scenes menu with 3-4 prebuilt scenarios (for example volcano island, refinery fire, ice cave, alchemist's flask) that load instantly. Hover readout of the element under the cursor (and temperature if modelled). The first frame must already show a scene in motion (load a scenario and pre-run ticks). Desktop: mouse paints, right-click or Shift erases. Touch: drag paints.
